module.title: Unit 5: Business Travel, Hotel Bookings & Airport Logistics
module.objective: Mampu melakukan koordinasi perjalanan dinas, check-in, dan penanganan keterlambatan transportasi secara percaya diri.

subModules.title: Reading Mission: Business Travel, Hotel Bookings and Airport Logistics
subModules.grammarFocus: Polite Requests with 'Would like to' and 'Could you', Managing Delays with 'I am afraid'
subModules.vocabularyFocus: Airport procedures, hotel amenities, travel schedules, and business itineraries

content.summary: In this reading mission, you will read an authentic business travel update and an email exchange between a travelling manager and a hotel receptionist. You will learn how to scan flight schedules, understand polite check-in conversations, and respond to sudden flight delays.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Polite requests with 'would like to', polite questions with 'Could you' or 'Would it be possible to', and bad-news markers with 'I am afraid' or 'Unfortunately'.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: reservation, boarding pass, layover, complimentary, itinerary, delayed, connecting flight, shuttle service, late check-out.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Scanning for times, flight codes, and hotel conditions, and identifying tone and polite formulas in business correspondence.

learningObjectives: Understand the main idea of a business travel itinerary and an urgent hotel communication.
Locate specific details such as flight arrival times, transfer options, and check-in policies.
Recognize and practice grammar patterns with polite requests and diplomatic notifications.

contextWarmup.prompt: You arrive at your hotel at 11:00 PM because your flight was delayed. What is the most polite way to request your room key?
options: Good evening. I'd like to check in, please. I have a reservation under the name Hartono.
Give me my room key right now because my flight was late.
I want a room immediately, my name is Hartono.
contextWarmup.explanation: Using 'I'd like to check in, please' is polite, professional, and standard when speaking with hotel staff.

rules: Use 'Subject + would like to + base verb' (or the contraction 'I'd like to') to express polite requests instead of using blunt phrases like 'I want'.
Use 'Could you + base verb...?' or 'Would it be possible to + base verb...?' when asking airline or hotel staff for assistance or special arrangements.
Use 'I'm afraid + clause' or 'Unfortunately + clause' to deliver unpleasant news gently, often followed by a recommendation with 'should' or 'had better'.

commonTrap.trapTitle: Direct Demands vs. Polite B1 Business Formulas
commonTrap.explanation: Learners often translate directly from casual language by saying 'I want to check out late' or 'You must change my ticket'. In international business travel, this sounds impolite. Use modal expressions like 'Could you' or 'Would it be possible to'.
commonTrap.wrong: I want a late check-out because my flight is delayed.
commonTrap.correct: Would it be possible to arrange a late check-out? My flight has been delayed.

content.passageTitle: Business Trip Disruption: Managing Flights and Hotel Check-in
paragraphs: David Hartono is a regional sales director travelling from Jakarta to Munich for an international trade exhibition. According to his original travel itinerary, he had an easy departure from Soekarno-Hatta International Airport, followed by a three-hour layover at Changi Airport in Singapore. From there, he planned to board his long-haul connecting flight to Germany and arrive at his hotel before noon.

However, unpredictable tropical storms disrupted schedules across Southeast Asia. At the departure gate in Jakarta, the airline announced that his initial flight was delayed by two and a half hours. David realized immediately that his connection in Singapore was at risk. He opened his smartphone to review his boarding pass and contact the Grand Central Hotel in Munich, where he had reserved a deluxe room for four nights.

David wrote a polite email to the hotel reception: 'Dear Front Desk Team, I have a reservation under the name David Hartono, booking reference GH-4092. I'd like to inform you that my flight from Jakarta has been delayed, so I will miss my original connecting flight. Could you please hold my room for a late check-in? I expect to reach the hotel around 9:00 PM instead of 11:30 AM.'

Within twenty minutes, the hotel manager sent a reassuring reply: 'Dear Mr Hartono, thank you for contacting us. We have updated your reservation notes. Your room is secured, and we also offer a complimentary airport shuttle service from Munich Airport every half hour. Please proceed to the shuttle station outside Terminal 1 upon arrival. Have a safe flight.'

connectedSpeech.note: The final consonant /k/ links directly into the following vowel sound /ɪ/.
The /d/ sound merges with the /j/ sound to produce a soft /dʒ/.
The vowel in 'was' reduces to a weak schwa /ə/ before the hard consonant.
A natural glide /j/ bridges the two vowel sounds between 'coffee' and 'in'.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Business Travel, Hotel Bookings & Airport Logistics

content.summary: This writing guide covers standard formulas for business travel correspondence, hotel arrangements, and transport delay notifications. You will learn how to state your requests politely, make formal inquiries, and communicate unexpected schedule changes with clear recommendations.

blueprintItems.title: Polite Travel Requests with Would Like To
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + would like to + base verb (+ complement)
blueprintItems.example: I would like to confirm our company booking for three single rooms from May 12th to May 15th.

blueprintItems.title: Formal Requests for Assistance
blueprintItems.formula: Could you + base verb ...? / Would it be possible to + base verb ...?
blueprintItems.example: Would it be possible to arrange an airport shuttle service for our arrival at Terminal 2?

blueprintItems.title: Reporting Delays and Recommending Solutions
blueprintItems.formula: Unfortunately / I am afraid + [delay clause] + Subject + should / had better + base verb
blueprintItems.example: I am afraid our flight has been delayed by two hours, so we had better notify the client immediately.

mechanicsRules.rule: Capitalize flight codes, airline names, and airport terminal designations properly.
mechanicsRules.badExample: our flight ga402 lands at changi airport terminal 3 on wednesday.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Our flight GA402 lands at Changi Airport Terminal 3 on Wednesday.
mechanicsRules.why: Airlines, flight numbers, airport terminals, and days are proper nouns and official codes.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use a comma after introductory discourse markers such as 'Unfortunately' or 'In addition' at the beginning of a sentence.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Unfortunately our connection in Frankfurt was cancelled.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Unfortunately, our connection in Frankfurt was cancelled.
mechanicsRules.why: Introductory transitional adverbs require a comma to separate them from the main clause.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use the bare infinitive after 'had better', not a full infinitive with 'to'.
mechanicsRules.badExample: You had better to take an earlier train to avoid airport traffic.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: You had better take an earlier train to avoid airport traffic.
mechanicsRules.why: 'Had better' functions like a modal auxiliary verb and must be followed directly by a base verb without 'to'.

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 1: Email for Late Hotel Check-In
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write three to four sentences to a hotel front desk. State your booking name, explain that your flight has been delayed, give your new expected arrival time, and ask politely if they can hold your room.
guidedLabChallenges.example: Dear Hotel Reception, I have a reservation under the name Maya Salim for tonight. Unfortunately, my flight has been delayed by two hours, so I expect to arrive at 11:30 p.m. Could you please hold my room until I arrive? Thank you for your assistance.
guidedLabChallenges.placeholder: Dear Reception, I have a booking under...

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 2: Travel Delay Update to a Business Partner
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write three to four sentences to your client or business host. Explain that you experienced airport transit delays, state your updated schedule, and suggest rescheduling your afternoon meeting.
guidedLabChallenges.example: Dear Mr. Davis, I am afraid our morning connection in Frankfurt was cancelled due to bad weather. We have been rebooked on an afternoon flight, so we had better postpone our 2:00 p.m. meeting until tomorrow morning. Would 9:30 a.m. tomorrow work for you?
guidedLabChallenges.placeholder: Dear Mr. Davis, I am writing to inform you that...

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the direct request into a formal request using 'I would like to':
practicumQuestions.promptText: I want to reserve a conference room for tomorrow morning.
practicumQuestions.hint: Replace 'I want to' with 'I would like to'.
targetAnswers: I would like to reserve a conference room for tomorrow morning.
I'd like to reserve a conference room for tomorrow morning.
practicumQuestions.explanation: In business correspondence, 'would like to' replaces 'want to' to sound polite and professional.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Transform this direct question into a polite request starting with 'Could you':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Send me the updated flight itinerary.
practicumQuestions.hint: Begin with 'Could you' and end with a question mark.
targetAnswers: Could you send me the updated flight itinerary?
Could you please send me the updated flight itinerary?
practicumQuestions.explanation: Starting a request with 'Could you' softens an imperative command into a standard business request.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Combine the two sentences using 'because' to explain the reason for rescheduling:
practicumQuestions.promptText: We must reschedule our hotel check-in. Our flight from Jakarta has been delayed.
practicumQuestions.hint: Join the clauses with 'because' without using a comma.
targetAnswers: We must reschedule our hotel check-in because our flight from Jakarta has been delayed.
We have to reschedule our hotel check-in because our flight from Jakarta has been delayed.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The conjunction 'because' introduces the cause of the rescheduling directly after the main clause.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence into a formal inquiry starting with 'Would it be possible to':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Can we check in early at 11:00 a.m.?
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'Would it be possible to check in early at 11:00 a.m.?'
targetAnswers: Would it be possible to check in early at 11:00 a.m.?
Would it be possible to check in early at 11:00 am?
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Would it be possible to + base verb' is a formal construction used for asking special permissions or services.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the punctuation, grammar, and capitalization mistakes in this sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: unfortunately flight sq951 is cancelled so you had better to contact singapore airlines immediately
practicumQuestions.hint: Add a comma after 'Unfortunately', capitalize flight codes and airline names, and omit 'to' after 'had better'.
targetAnswers: Unfortunately, flight SQ951 is cancelled, so you had better contact Singapore Airlines immediately.
Unfortunately, flight SQ951 is cancelled so you had better contact Singapore Airlines immediately.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Unfortunately' needs a following comma, proper nouns must be capitalized, and 'had better' is followed by a base verb without 'to'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Deliver this bad news professionally starting with 'I am afraid':
practicumQuestions.promptText: The airport shuttle is no longer running tonight.
practicumQuestions.hint: Introduce the clause with 'I am afraid that' or 'I am afraid'.
targetAnswers: I am afraid that the airport shuttle is no longer running tonight.
I am afraid the airport shuttle is no longer running tonight.
I'm afraid that the airport shuttle is no longer running tonight.
I'm afraid the airport shuttle is no longer running tonight.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'I am afraid (that)' softens negative announcements in business travel contexts.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Combine these two sentences into one sentence using 'so':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Our baggage was delayed in Tokyo. We had better buy basic toiletries for tonight.
practicumQuestions.hint: Connect the result clause with ', so'.
targetAnswers: Our baggage was delayed in Tokyo, so we had better buy basic toiletries for tonight.
Our baggage was delayed in Tokyo so we had better buy basic toiletries for tonight.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The conjunction 'so' shows the logical consequence of the delayed baggage.

practicumQuestions.promptText: could you confirm if breakfast is included in room 402 at grand hyatt hotel
practicumQuestions.hint: Capitalize the first word, the hotel name, and finish with a question mark.
targetAnswers: Could you confirm if breakfast is included in room 402 at Grand Hyatt Hotel?
Could you confirm if breakfast is included in Room 402 at Grand Hyatt Hotel?
practicumQuestions.explanation: Sentences must start with a capital letter, hotel names are proper nouns requiring capitalization, and inquiries end with a question mark.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write a complete sentence advising your colleague to take the express train instead of a taxi, using 'had better':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Advise your colleague: take the express train instead of a taxi to avoid missing the flight.
targetAnswers: You had better take the express train instead of a taxi to avoid missing the flight.
We had better take the express train instead of a taxi to avoid missing the flight.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Had better + base verb' gives strong advice to prevent a negative outcome like missing a flight.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write a polite one-sentence request asking the hotel staff if they can store your luggage after check-out:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Ask the receptionist politely to store your luggage after check-out.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'Could you please store...' or 'Would it be possible to store...'
targetAnswers: Could you please store our luggage after check-out?
Could you please store my luggage after check-out?
Would it be possible to store our luggage after check-out?
Would it be possible to store my luggage after check-out?
practicumQuestions.explanation: Using 'Could you please...' or 'Would it be possible to...' forms a courteous request suitable for hotel staff.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Business Travel and Airport Communication

content.summary: Practise clear, polite English for business travel. Give important details slowly, such as your name, booking reference, flight number, and travel times. Use complete sentences when asking for help or explaining a problem.
content.audioGuidance: Use a calm pace at the hotel desk and airport. Stress key information words, such as the date, destination, and flight number. Let your voice rise for polite yes-or-no questions, and fall at the end of statements and information questions.

pillars.name: Vowel Clarity
pillars.explanation: Say the vowel sounds in words such as 'ship' and 'sheep' clearly. This helps listeners understand important travel details.

pillars.name: Word Stress
pillars.explanation: Give the stressed syllable more energy in words such as 'reservation' and 'itinerary'. Practise each word slowly before using it in a sentence.

pillars.name: Polite Questions
pillars.explanation: Ask for help with phrases such as 'Could you check my booking, please?' Keep your tone polite and make the request easy to understand.

pillars.name: Natural Rhythm
pillars.explanation: Pause briefly between pieces of information. For example, say the flight number first, then explain the problem.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: The stress changes from the second syllable in 'reserve' to the third syllable in 'reservation'.
Stress the second syllable in 'itinerary' and the first syllable in 'travel'.
The stress is on 'men' in 'complimentary' but on 'com' in 'compliment'.
The main stress stays on the second syllable when '-ed' is added.

drills.targetText: I have a reservation for three nights under the name Widodo.
drills.phonetic: /aɪ hæv ə ˌrezəˈveɪʃən fə θriː naɪts ˈʌndə ðə neɪm wɪˈdoʊdoʊ/
drills.focus: Stress in 'reservation' and clear delivery of a guest name
drills.hint: Say the name clearly, and stress the third syllable of 'reservation'.

drills.targetText: Please have your boarding pass and passport ready.
drills.phonetic: /pliːz hæv jə ˈbɔːdɪŋ pɑːs ən ˈpɑːspɔːt ˈredi/
drills.hint: Pause briefly after 'boarding pass' so both documents are clear.

drills.targetText: Our flight is delayed, so I may miss my connection.
drills.phonetic: /aʊə flaɪt ɪz dɪˈleɪd səʊ aɪ meɪ mɪs maɪ kəˈnekʃən/
drills.focus: Word stress and explaining a travel problem
drills.hint: Stress 'delayed' and 'miss' to make the problem clear.

drills.targetText: Could you email me the updated itinerary, please?
drills.phonetic: /kʊd juː ˈiːmeɪl miː ði ʌpˈdeɪtɪd aɪˈtɪnərəri pliːz/
drills.hint: Use a friendly tone, and stress 'email' and the second syllable of 'itinerary'.

roleplay.context: You are checking in at a hotel during a business trip. Confirm your reservation and ask about breakfast and the airport shuttle.

turns.speaker: Hotel Receptionist
turns.text: Good evening. Do you have a reservation with us?
turns.translation: Selamat malam. Apakah Anda memiliki reservasi di tempat kami?

turns.speaker: Business Traveller
turns.text: Yes, I have a reservation for three nights under the name Widodo.
turns.translation: Ya, saya memiliki reservasi untuk tiga malam atas nama Widodo.

turns.speaker: Hotel Receptionist
turns.text: Thank you. Breakfast is complimentary, and the airport shuttle leaves at six thirty.
turns.translation: Terima kasih. Sarapan gratis, dan shuttle bandara berangkat pukul enam tiga puluh.

turns.speaker: Business Traveller
turns.text: That is helpful. Could you confirm my check-out time, please?
turns.translation: Informasi itu sangat membantu. Bisakah Anda memastikan waktu check-out saya?

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 30 seconds about a business trip you have taken or would like to take.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Describe a business trip and explain how you would organise the main parts of your travel.
storyPoints: Say where you would travel and why the trip is important.
Describe your flight and hotel arrangements.
Explain what you would include in your itinerary.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: I would book my flight and hotel early, then email my itinerary to my colleagues.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /aɪ wʊd bʊk maɪ flaɪt ən həʊˈtel ˈɜːli ðen ˈiːmeɪl maɪ aɪˈtɪnərəri tə maɪ ˈkɒliːɡz/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use complete sentences and give the details in a clear order.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 30 seconds about a delay or travel problem and how you would respond.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Imagine your flight is delayed and you may miss a connecting flight. Tell the story of what you would do.
storyPoints: Explain which flight is delayed and where you are going.
Say who you would contact and what information you would ask for.
Describe how you would update your hotel or colleagues.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: If my flight were delayed, I would contact the airline and update my colleagues.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ɪf maɪ flaɪt wə dɪˈleɪd aɪ wʊd ˈkɒntækt ði ˈeəlaɪn ən ʌpˈdeɪt maɪ ˈkɒliːɡz/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Explain the problem and your next steps using a calm, clear voice.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Take part in a live roleplay. Confirm your booking and ask a follow-up question.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: You are at a hotel reception desk. Speak to the receptionist and check in for your stay.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You arrive at a hotel for a work trip. You have a reservation for three nights under your name, and you want to confirm whether breakfast is included.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a business traveller. Give your name, confirm the reservation, and politely ask about breakfast.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Give your booking details clearly and ask a polite question.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Take part in a live roleplay. Ask for help finding your gate.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Speak to an airport staff member after passing security.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are at the airport and cannot find the gate for your flight. You have your boarding pass and need clear directions.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a passenger. Tell the staff member your flight number and ask where the gate is.
practicumQuestions.explanation: State your flight details and make a clear, polite request.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Take part in a live roleplay. Explain the delay and ask about your options.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Call the airline help desk because your flight has been delayed.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: Your flight has been delayed and you have a connecting flight later that day. You need to know whether you can still make the connection.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a traveller speaking to an airline representative. Give your flight details and ask what you should do next.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Explain the situation briefly, then ask a direct question about your options.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Take part in a live roleplay call. Update a colleague and confirm the travel plan.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Call a colleague to discuss your hotel, airport transfer, and travel schedule.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are coordinating a business trip with a colleague. Your hotel offers a complimentary airport shuttle, and you need to confirm the arrival time and itinerary.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are the traveller. Explain the shuttle plan, confirm the arrival time, and ask your colleague to check the itinerary.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Share key information in a sensible order and check that the plan is understood.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say one clear sentence for each word: reservation, boarding pass, layover, complimentary, itinerary, and delayed.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Use these travel words in complete sentences: reservation, boarding pass, layover, complimentary, itinerary, and delayed.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: My itinerary shows a two-hour layover, and my flight is not delayed.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use each word in a sentence that shows its meaning.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Make polite requests using 'Could you...?' and 'Would you...?' in a hotel or airport situation.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Ask someone to confirm your reservation, check your flight, and explain the shuttle schedule.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Could you confirm my reservation, please?
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use a question form and a polite word such as 'please' when asking for help.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say 'reservation', 'itinerary', 'complimentary', and 'delayed'. Give extra stress to the correct syllable in each word.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Repeat these words clearly: reservation, itinerary, complimentary, delayed.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: My reservation and itinerary are ready, but my flight is delayed.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˌrezəˈveɪʃən ən aɪˈtɪnərəri ɑː ˈredi bət maɪ flaɪt ɪz dɪˈleɪd/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Listen for the stressed syllable in each word and keep the other syllables lighter.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say one polite yes-or-no question with rising intonation and one information question with falling intonation.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Practise the difference between a rising yes-or-no question and a falling information question.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Is breakfast complimentary? Where does the airport shuttle leave from?
practicumQuestions.explanation: Let your voice rise at the end of the yes-or-no question and fall at the end of the information question.
